$grammar_comment: THE GRAMMAR IS LOAD-BEARING AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE REFERENCE CONSUMER'S TOOL ASSUMES.
The live canonical is a SINGLE-SPRINT SCALAR-HEADER document: top-level `sprint: 291`,
`status: in_progress`, then a `stories:` mapping. The reference consumer's own rotation tool
(generate-sprint-status.py) is written against a MONOLITH grammar of col-0 block keys
The two grammars are DISJOINT: that regex matches ZERO lines in either live canonical, so
--close-sweep silently no-ops and exits 0 while reporting success. Verified by running it.
Worse, that regex DOES match `sprint_291_housekeeping:` and yields group(1)=291 -- so the moment
a housekeeping block exists, the tool mistakes it for the sprint block, deletes the closure
evidence Check 3 needs, and leaves the rows un-pruned. That is why the housekeeping key is
matched here by an ANCHORED, EXPLICIT pattern that cannot collide with a sprint block key.
Enforce ONLY the STRUCTURE a reader depends on -- `sprint` is an integer, `status` is present --
never the historical FORMAT. Real consumer files carry inline `# comments`, block scalars, and
free-form prose in closure_evidence. A stricter pattern here re-creates the wedge this change
exists to remove: a linter that errors on real data on first contact gets turned off.
$story_grammar_comment: THE STORY-ENTRY GRAMMAR IS DELIBERATELY INDENT-RELATIVE AND ID-BLIND, and both halves are
there because the reference consumer's three attempts at this check each went VACUOUSLY GREEN
on the half it fixed the other way.
ID-BLIND. A story entry is ANY key of the `stories:` mapping. There is no id pattern here on
purpose: the consumer's validator globs `story-<N>-*` and its live corpus is named
`story-S<N>-*` and `s<N>-<M>`, so its discovery loop matched zero files and it reported
'checked 0 story files' as a success line. A pattern that matches only one naming convention
IS the vacuous-green defect; the mapping key is the id, whatever it is spelled.
INDENT-RELATIVE. Entry keys sit at whatever indent the file's first entry uses, and fields sit
deeper than that. Pinning two literal indents would make a two-space file and a four-space file
disagree about whether a document has any stories at all -- the same class of silent zero.
A key line carries nothing after the colon; a field line carries a value. Lines deeper than the
field indent (block-scalar continuations, the long `note:` values real trees carry) are never
The COUNT is part of the contract. `sprint-status.sh check-stories` prints how many entries it
parsed and how many comparisons it made, and exits non-zero on zero -- see $story_check_comment.
$story_check_comment: The mechanical half of gate-validation.md Check 5 ('Story status consistency?'), which stated
'Run: Read both files, compare status values programmatically' while core shipped no program.
The join: for every entry of the current sprint's `stories:` mapping, in each canonical copy
that exists, the entry's `status:` MUST equal the status in the story FILE that entry names.
Story-file status is read from YAML frontmatter first and from the `**Status:**` body header
only when the file carries no frontmatter block -- both spellings are live in a real corpus
(measured over the reference consumer's 988 story files: 343 carry a frontmatter `status:`,
726 carry a `**Status:**` header, 109 carry both, 28 carry neither).
The body header's value is taken up to its first sentence break because real entries continue
into prose ('done (all 3 gates green)'); the frontmatter value is compared verbatim.
An entry whose file cannot be resolved, or whose file yields no status at all, is a FINDING and
never a skip. Skipping is how the consumer's version reported success on a corpus it could not

status.desc: the story's status; MUST equal the status in the story file this entry names (Check 5)

file.desc: path to the story file, relative to the canonical's own directory. Absent -> the entry key's sprint-stripped stem is globbed against the resolved stories_dir.

$story_file_comment: `stories_dir` IS A TEMPLATE, NOT A PATH. `{sprint}` is substituted with the sprint number to
name one sprint's corpus, or with `*` to name every sprint's at once -- artifact-path-grammar.md
rule 1 declares `s*` the same reserved slot quantified over every sprint, so the two readings are
one declaration rather than two keys that drift apart.
IT CARRIES THE SPRINT SLOT BECAUSE THE FILENAME NO LONGER DOES, and that is the whole point.
Under the flat layout the sprint lived in the basename, which made the corpus unjudgeable: 758 of

-- character-for-character the `story-<M>-<slug>.md` the grammar prescribes, where `<M>` is the
story INDEX. No expression separates those two readings. A directory does, and the sprint is
NO SHIPPED PROGRAM MAY RESTATE THE RESOLVED LITERAL. This key is the only home; I84 in

$fields_comment: `status: done` is the ONE value with mechanical meaning: it is the predicate route.md Step 6
reads to decide a new sprint has started (done -> N+1, anything else -> N, i.e. a re-plan of the
sprint still in flight). Every other value is free-form and deliberately un-enumerated -- the
reference consumer uses `in_progress`, and constraining the enum here would wedge any consumer

sprint.desc: integer sprint number -- the pipeline's sprint identity

status.desc: sprint envelope status; `done` means closed (route.md Step 6 reads this to derive N+1). Any other value means in-flight.

variant.desc: pipeline variant this sprint was routed as (documentary)

$housekeeping_comment: The close envelope. Written ONLY by `sprint-status.sh close`, read by validate-mandatory-rules.sh
Check 3 at retro Step 5c. `closure_evidence` is free-form prose by design -- the reference
consumer's real entries run to several hundred characters of PR/deploy/smoke-test narrative.
Check 3 asserts it is NON-EMPTY, never that it matches a shape.

envelope_status.desc: always `done` -- the block exists only at close

closure_evidence.desc: non-empty prose: what proves the sprint closed (PRs, deploys, smoke tests, operator validation)

header_lines: The sprint envelope + per-story execution ledger. ONE canonical copy, at
**Schema is canonical in `.claude/schemas/sprint-status.json`.** This header is
RENDERED from it by `scripts/ai-dlc/sprint-status.sh --render` and byte-checked by
`--check`. Do NOT hand-edit this region — edit the schema and re-render.
- `sprint: <N>` — integer sprint number. REQUIRED. The pipeline's sprint identity;
`route.md` Step 6 derives it mechanically via `sprint-status.sh sprint-id`.
- `status: <value>` — REQUIRED. `done` means the sprint is closed; any other value
means in-flight. Only `done` carries mechanical meaning.
- `stories:` — a MAPPING keyed by normalized story id (`story-<N>-<M>:`). NOT a list:
a list form matches no reader and reports vacuous-green all sprint.
- `sprint_<N>_housekeeping:` — the close envelope, written ONLY by
Rotation is MECHANICAL and happens at pipeline START, not at close: `sprint-status.sh
roll` freezes the closed sprint to `s<N>/sprint-status.yaml` and writes the new
envelope in ONE atomic step. This is why the closed sprint's `status: done` stays
readable until its successor exists — which is exactly what Step 6 reads.
